issues.span:
Having known oneself to have faults and others too
To be an ocean of good qualities
issues.evidence: བདག་ཉིད་སྐྱོན་བཅས་གཞན་ལ་ཡང་། ཡོན་ཏན་རྒྱ་མཚོར་ཤེས་བྱས་ནས། — "too" (ཡང་) goes with others as an ocean of good qualities (Sanskrit parān api guṇodadhīn; bo-kunpal 8-112 gives self = faults, others = qualities); the English can be read as "oneself and others too have faults".
issues.fix: Having known that oneself has faults, and that others too are oceans of good qualities,

issues.evidence: བདག་མེད་ལུས་འདི་ལ། — བདག་མེད་ modifies ལུས་ ("this body that is selfless/without self"; Sanskrit svakāye 'smin nirātmake; bo-shenga 8-114 བདག་མེད་པའི་ལུས་). "Body of selflessness" implies the body belongs to selflessness.
issues.fix: this body, which is selfless (lacks a self)

issues.evidence: འཁོར་གྱི་འཇིགས་པའང་བསལ་བའི་ཕྱིར། — the suffix འང "even" (Sanskrit pariṣacchāradyabhayam api) marks even the minor fear of timidity in assemblies (bo-kunpal 8-117 "བག་ཚ་བ་ཙམ་གྱི་འཇིགས་པའང་"); the English places "even" only on the name.
issues.fix: In order to dispel even wandering beings' fear in assemblies,

issues.span: be hostile as toward an enemy
issues.evidence: སྡང་མི་བྱེད། — སྡང་བ is "to hate/loathe" (Sanskrit na dviṣet; bo-kunpal 8-120 སྡང་བར་མི་བྱེད།), not "be hostile".

issues.span: Will thereby be burned in the Avīci hell;
issues.evidence: དེས་ནི་མནར་མེད་བསྲེག་འགྱུར་ན། — the clause ends in the conditional ན ("if"; bo-kunpal 8-122 ends "འགྱུར་ན"), continuing into 8-123's question. The English states it as an independent assertion.
issues.fix: If one is thereby burned in the Avīci hell,

issues.evidence: ལྷ་ཡི་ཆོས། — ཆོས here is "nature/way" parallel to འདྲེ་ཡི་ཚུལ (Sanskrit devarājatā "godliness"; bo-kunpal 8-124 ཆོས་ལུགས་བཟང་པོ, bo-shenga ལྷ་ཡི་རྒྱུར་གྱུར་པའི་ཆོས). "Dharma" suggests the Buddhist teaching.
